title: Cohomology of unbounded complexes
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $K\in D(X_{\Et})$, and $\mathcal B$ a class
of objects of $X_{\Et}$ such that (1) every object of $X_{\Et}$
admits a covering by objects of $\mathcal B$, and (2)
$H^p(U_{\Et},\mathcal H^q(K))=0$ for all $p>0$, all
$q\in\mathbf Z$, and all $U\in\mathcal B$. Then
$H^q(U_{\Et},K)=H^0(U_{\Et},\mathcal H^q(K))$ for all $q$ and all
$U\in\mathcal B$. (*Source:* Stacks Project,
[Tag
`0BKZ`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BKZ).)

proof.text: Use the small representatives of the sites fixed by [def-weil-size-convention], and regard abelian sheaves as modules over the constant ring sheaf $\mathbf Z_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Explicitly, on a cover where a section of $\mathbf Z_X$ is represented by integers, let it act by repeated addition on the restrictions of a section of the abelian sheaf. These local sections agree on overlaps and glue uniquely; the module axioms and compatibility with restriction hold locally for integers and hence globally. Conversely any $\mathbf Z_X$-action must be this action. Every abelian-sheaf morphism commutes with it, so this is an equivalence with the same underlying complexes, cohomology and homotopies. Write $H^r(U,L)$ for the cohomology of derived evaluation at the object $U$ of $X_{\Et}$, whose degree-zero recipe is [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. This is the notation $H^r(U_{\Et},L|_U)$ in the statement, also for unbounded $L$: by [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-injectives] restriction to $X_{\Et}/U$ is exact, so it preserves quasi-isomorphisms, and by [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized] it preserves K-injectives. Consequently, restricting a K-injective resolution $L\to I$ and then evaluating at the final object of the slice gives exactly the complex $I(U)$. The covering-preserving equivalence $X_{\Et}/U\simeq U_{\Et}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open] identifies this final object with $U$. An equivalence of abelian categories preserves kernels, cokernels and homotopies by their defining universal properties, hence preserves acyclic complexes and K-injectives. Therefore the same complex computes derived global sections on $U_{\Et}$ by [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded]. In particular hypothesis (2) is precisely $R^p\Gamma(U,\mathcal H^r K)=0$ for $p>0$.

proof.text:
Put $K_n=\tau_{\geq-n}K$ for $n\in\mathbf N$, with transitions $t_n:K_{n+1}\to K_n$. The good-truncation construction [def-kun-truncations] gives $\mathcal H^r(K_n)=0$ for $r<-n$ and the canonical identification $\mathcal H^r(K_n)=\mathcal H^r(K)$ for $r\geq-n$. Fix $U\in\mathcal B$. Apply [thm-sp-truncation-e2] to the bounded-below complex $K_n$, with $v=\Gamma(U,-)$ and lower bound $-n$. Its source category and its target $\operatorname{Ab}$ are Grothendieck: apply [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] to the constant $\mathbf Z$-ringed small site $X_{\Et}$, and to the site with one object, only its identity and the trivial topology, respectively. On the latter site a module sheaf is just an abelian group. Evaluation is additive left exact by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and the K-injective recipe in the cited existence theorem supplies the derived functor required by the spectral-sequence theorem. We obtain a convergent spectral sequence with finite abutment filtration
$$E_2^{p,r}(n)=H^p(U,\mathcal H^r(K_n))\Longrightarrow H^{p+r}(U,K_n).$$
Only bounded-below complexes are used here.

source.place: Tag 0BKZ, label lemma-cohomology-over-U-trivial; bounded-below spectral sequence, from Derived Categories Tag 015J, label lemma-two-ss-complex-functor

proof.text:
All terms with $p<0$ vanish by the spectral-sequence theorem, and those with $p>0$ vanish by hypothesis (2) and the cohomology calculation for $K_n$ in step 2. Every differential $d_s$ for $s\geq2$ out of column zero lands in column $s>0$, and every differential into it starts in column $-s<0$. Thus $E_\infty^{0,r}(n)=E_2^{0,r}(n)$ and all other columns are zero. The finite decreasing filtration on $H^r(U,K_n)$ has $F^0=H^r(U,K_n)$; all its graded pieces with positive index are zero, so its finite zero end implies $F^1=0$. Its column-zero edge therefore gives an isomorphism
$$e_{n,r}:H^r(U,K_n)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(U,\mathcal H^r(K_n)).$$
These are compatible with $t_n$: the maps of canonical truncations commute with $t_n$, so the images defining $F^p$, the cycle and boundary kernels and quotients defining the pages, and the column-zero quotient maps all commute with $t_n$. The $E_2$ identifications in [thm-sp-truncation-e2] are natural. Hence
$$e_{n,r}\circ H^r(U,t_n)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal H^r(t_n))\circ e_{n+1,r}.$$
This verifies compatibility of the actual transition maps, rather than only abstract equality of the groups.

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-kun-site-truncation-derived-limit] hold for $\mathcal C=X_{\Et}$, $\mathcal O=\mathbf Z_X$, $E=K$ and $d=0$. Smallness is fixed in step 1; hypothesis (1) is exactly its covering assumption, and hypothesis (2) implies the required vanishing for every $p>0$ and $r<0$. It follows that $K$, with the canonical projections $K\to K_n$, is a derived limit of $(K_n,t_n)$. No bound on all sheaves on $X_{\Et}$ is being assumed; only the specified cohomology sheaves of $K$ enter this application.

source.place: Tag 0BKZ, label lemma-cohomology-over-U-trivial; first sentence of the source proof, applying Tag 0D6P with d=0

proof.text:
Apply [lem-kun-site-rgamma-derived-limit] to the derived-limit triangle of step 4 and to the fixed object $U$. It says that $R\Gamma(U,K)$ is a derived limit of the tower $R\Gamma(U,K_n)$ in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$, with projections obtained from $K\to K_n$. Now [lem-pc-derived-limit-milnor-sequence], applied in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$, gives, for each integer $r$, the exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow R^1\varprojlim_n H^{r-1}(U,K_n)\longrightarrow H^r(U,K)\longrightarrow\varprojlim_n H^r(U,K_n)\longrightarrow0.$$
There is no quasi-compactness or finiteness hypothesis in either cited statement.

proof.text: Choose $N\in\mathbf N$ with $N\geq1-r$. For $n\geq N$ and $j\in\{r-1,r\}$, good truncation gives $\mathcal H^j(K_n)=\mathcal H^j(K)$, and the map $\mathcal H^j(t_n)$ is the identity under these canonical identifications: its composite with the canonical projection from $\mathcal H^j(K)$ is that same projection. Use the compatible edge isomorphisms of step 3. The two towers $H^j(U,K_n)$ are therefore eventually constant, with identity transition maps on their tails identified with $\Gamma(U,\mathcal H^j(K))$.

source.place: Tag 0BKZ, label lemma-cohomology-over-U-trivial; last two sentences of the source proof, with a common threshold for r and r-1

proof.text:
For completeness compute the limits of either eventually constant tower $(A_n,f_n)$. The Roos formula of [lem-pc-derived-limit-roos-abelian-groups] identifies $\varprojlim A_n$ with the kernel and $R^1\varprojlim A_n$ with the cokernel of
$$1-s:\prod_nA_n\to\prod_nA_n,\qquad (x_n)\mapsto(x_n-f_n(x_{n+1})).$$
Choose $N$ after which all $f_n$ are isomorphisms. Given any $(b_n)$, set $x_N=0$, define $x_{n+1}=f_n^{-1}(x_n-b_n)$ for $n\geq N$, and then define $x_n=b_n+f_n(x_{n+1})$ backwards for $n<N$. This solves $(1-s)x=b$, so the cokernel is zero. In the kernel, $x_N$ uniquely determines every later entry using the inverse transitions and every earlier entry using the transitions; thus projection to $A_N$ is an isomorphism, and in the identified constant tail it is the common value. Applying this to the two towers in step 6 makes the left term of step 5 zero and identifies its right term with $\Gamma(U,\mathcal H^r(K))$. Exactness gives
$$H^r(U_{\Et},K)\cong H^0(U_{\Et},\mathcal H^r(K)).$$
Since $r\in\mathbf Z$ and $U\in\mathcal B$ were arbitrary, this is the claimed equality in the canonical cohomological identifications.

tool_uses.why: Exact restriction to a slice is a general site tool needed to interpret cohomology over an etale object.
K-injective restriction identifies object evaluation with unbounded cohomology on the localized site.
The localized small etale site at any etale object is the small etale site of its scheme.
General bounded-below hypercohomology convergence and its finite filtration; the Kunneth unit has no separate convergence theorem.
Grothendieck and K-injective existence hypotheses for the bounded-below spectral-sequence tool.
General Milnor short exact sequence in D(Ab), after the new site theorem puts derived sections in that situation.
General kernel/cokernel computation used to prove the eventually constant inverse-limit calculation explicitly.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $K\in D(X_{\Et})$, and $\mathcal B$ a class
of objects of $X_{\Et}$ such that (1) every object of $X_{\Et}$
admits a covering by objects of $\mathcal B$, and (2)
$H^p(U_{\Et},\mathcal H^q(K))=0$ for all $p>0$, all
$q\in\mathbf Z$, and all $U\in\mathcal B$. Then
$H^q(U_{\Et},K)=H^0(U_{\Et},\mathcal H^q(K))$ for all $q$ and all
$U\in\mathcal B$.

proof.text:
For $U\in\mathcal B$ the hypercohomology spectral sequence of
[def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations] (in the global-section
form) has
$E_2^{p,q}=H^p(U_{\Et},\mathcal H^q(K))\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(U_{\Et},K)$. Hypothesis (2) kills the columns $p>0$, so
only the column $p=0$ survives and there are no differentials to or
from it; hence $H^n(U_{\Et},K)=E_2^{0,n}=H^0(U_{\Et},\mathcal H^n(K))$
for every $n$, which is the assertion, in the notation of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].
